summary: Map office processes, design Power Automate approvals, and control exceptions. Explore this practical five-day workflow automation course.
lede: Low-code workflow automation training shows operations, administrative, HR, and finance professionals how to turn recurring office tasks into documented, controlled workflows. Participants practise scoring automation candidates, mapping processes with BPMN 2.0, defining Power Automate triggers and approval routes, handling exceptions, and tracking workflow measures in Excel.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who own, support, or improve recurring administrative workflows. It suits office teams seeking practical low-code automation skills without a programming-focused curriculum. This course is designed for: Operations managers prioritizing repetitive service workflows for automation. Administrative supervisors documenting request handling and approval handoffs. HR operations specialists streamlining employee onboarding and personnel requests. Finance operations analysts automating invoice routing and payment approvals. Accounts payable coordinators tracking invoice exceptions and overdue approvals. Payroll operations staff controlling recurring input checks and sign-offs. Process improvement practitioners mapping administrative workflows with BPMN 2.0. Shared services team leads monitoring service requests and workflow backlogs. Business analysts documenting Power Automate requirements and acceptance tests. Government administration officers improving records-based internal service workflows.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with administrative or back-office processes and routine office software is useful. No coding or programming is required. Hands-on Power Automate activities require access to an appropriate organizational account; confirm availability and licensing before delivery.
